main_text.p: cornices temperamenti esse firmioris & fic-cioris,obque id longæuas,gaudereque plurimum frigidis atq; humectantib9. Tempesti-tes præsentiunt, vt & corui,quod Virgilius expressit carmine suo,

p.i: Tum cornix plena pluviam vocat improba voce, Et sola in ficca fecum spatiatur arena,
Antequam stantes repetat paludes, Imbrium diuina (præscia) aus[?] (cornix) immi-nentum.
Mutant cum tempestatibus vnà, Raucisonos cantus cornicum secla verusta Coruorumq; greges, ubi aquà dicuntur & imbres Poscere, & interdum ventos aurasq; vocare.

main_text.p: Nec prætereundum,in pluviarum denun-Cornicēsciatione cornicem contra naturam suam cro-& cornicitare voce crassa & rauca,coruos vero non in pluviisin pluviis rauca voce, sed purissima contra naturam denunci-suam[?],non solitarios,sed plures, pluviæ dareandi qua signum.vocē v-

Ad extremum carnes earum aeriæ pestisantur? tempore conferre plurimum creditur. quia Carnes venenis putredinique obsistunt, qualitatecoruorū cum manifesta, tum etiam antipatheticaveneno Manifesta est in ficco,& ad frigiditatem ver-aduer-gente temperamento, tale enim putredinemsantur, prohibet. Galenus & Philosophi ac Medici omnes.

page.notes: Page number read as 587; the scan is slightly blurred. Running head read as "PROROGANDA A.". Catchword "Expe-" and signature "Bb 2" read at the foot. Margin notes on the right are only partly legible: "Cornicēs", "& corni", "in pluviis", "andi qua", "vocē v-", "antur?", "coruorū", "veneno", "aduer-", "santur," are read from the scan, but their exact placement in the line is uncertain. The word "denunci-" and its continuation "suam" at the line break are doubtful. "aus" in the Horace quotation is doubtful. Verse lines are set in italic. Printed spelling is kept, including "verusta", "ficca", "fecum", "tempestatibus". Long s is normalised to s and u/v to the vowel or consonant form.
